ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Comparison of Randomized Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Analytically compare the expected sample efficiency of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP, derive non-asymptotic bounds for their sample complexities, and discuss their relationships to each other.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the bounds using linear and logistic regression models, and compare the theoretical results to results from existing estimators using real-world datasets.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis should reveal that LeverageSHAP generally has the best sample efficiency, but may be computationally expensive in high-dimensional settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Sampling Without Replacement for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of sampling without replacement (SNR) on the performance and sample efficiency of KernelSHAP. Specifically, analyze the trade-off between SNR and the number of samples required to achieve a given accuracy, using both real-world and synthetic datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of SNR to paired sampling and no sampling at all (i.e., full evaluation of v(S) for all subsets), and compare to the results of existing works that have already explored SNR.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: Implementing SNR in KernelSHAP may further improve its sample efficiency, but requires careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid over-sampling or under-sampling certain subsets.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating Sampling Without Replacement for KernelSHAP (revised)
PROPOSAL: REVISED description: Provide a detailed implementation of sampling without replacement (SNR) in KernelSHAP, including the development of a novel algorithm to efficiently handle the permutations of subsets when sampling without replacement. Experimentally evaluate SNR-KernelSHAP on a variety of real-world datasets, and compare its performance to existing sampling schemes.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of SNR-KernelSHAP to the results of KernelSHAP with paired sampling and no sampling at all, and analyze the effect of hyperparameter tuning on the performance of SNR-KernelSHAP.
COST: 105
PREDICTION: The proposed SNR approach should significantly improve the sample efficiency of KernelSHAP, especially for large datasets and high-dimensional features.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Improving Estimation Accuracy
PROPOSAL: Explore the possibility of using adversarial training to improve the estimation accuracy of randomized Shapley value estimators like KernelSHAP. In particular, generate adversarial examples for the estimator by attacking it with a learned perturbation function, and use the generated examples to train the estimator in a self-supervised manner.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of the adversarially trained estimator to the original KernelSHAP, and investigate the effect of the adversarial training on the sample efficiency and interpretability of the estimator.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The proposed adversarial training approach may improve the estimation accuracy of KernelSHAP, but requires careful exploration of the trade-off between robustness and sample efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Kernel Type on KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the choice of kernel type affects the performance of KernelSHAP on different datasets and models. Specifically, compare the results of KernelSHAP with different kernel types (e.g., linear, polynomial, Gaussian) on a variety of real-world datasets and models, and analyze the effect of the kernel type on the estimation accuracy and sample efficiency of KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of different kernel types to the results of no kernel (i.e., linear Shapley values), and analyze the trade-off between the computational cost of the kernel and its effect on the estimation accuracy and sample efficiency of KernelSHAP.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The choice of kernel type has a significant impact on the performance of KernelSHAP, and the best kernel type may vary depending on the dataset and model.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Kernel Type on KernelSHAP (revised)
PROPOSAL: REVISED description: Develop a novel approach to automatically selecting the best kernel type for KernelSHAP on a given dataset and model. Specifically, propose a hyperparameter tuning algorithm that searches over a set of predefined kernel types and selects the one that results in the highest estimation accuracy and lowest sample complexity. Evaluate the proposed approach on a variety of real-world datasets and models, and compare its performance to the results of hand-tuned kernel selection.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of the proposed approach to the results of no kernel selection (i.e., using a fixed kernel type for all datasets and models).
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should significantly improve the performance of KernelSHAP by automatically selecting the best kernel type for each dataset and model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: KernelSHAP for High-Dimensional Data with Feature Hashing
PROPOSAL: Develop a modified version of KernelSHAP that is specifically designed for high-dimensional data. The proposed approach uses feature hashing to reduce the dimensionality of the input data, and then applies KernelSHAP to the hashed features. Evaluate the proposed approach on a variety of high-dimensional datasets, and compare its performance to the results of standard KernelSHAP and other dimensionality reduction techniques.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of the proposed approach to the results of standard KernelSHAP and other dimensionality reduction techniques, such as PCA and t-SNE.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should significantly improve the performance of KernelSHAP on high-dimensional data by reducing the dimensionality of the input data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Estimating Shapley Values with a Hybrid Approach
PROPOSAL: Propose a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. Specifically, use LeverageSHAP to select a subset of the most important data points, and then apply KernelSHAP to these selected data points to estimate the Shapley values. Evaluate the proposed approach on a variety of datasets, and compare its performance to the results of standard KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of the proposed approach to the results of standard KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, and analyze the trade-off between the estimation accuracy and sample complexity of the proposed approach.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The proposed hybrid approach should significantly improve the performance of KernelSHAP on large and complex datasets by reducing the sample complexity and improving the estimation accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Convergence Rate of Randomized Shapley Value Estimators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the convergence rate of randomized Shapley value estimators such as KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. Specifically, analyze the effect of the number of samples on the convergence rate of these estimators, and derive theoretical bounds on the convergence rate. Evaluate the theoretical results using a variety of datasets and compare the convergence rates of the different estimators.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of the analysis to the results of existing works that have studied the convergence rate of these estimators.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The proposed analysis should provide valuable insights into the convergence rate of randomized Shapley value estimators, and help identify the optimal number of samples for these estimators.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a New Randomized Estimator for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Propose a new randomized estimator for Shapley values that combines the insights from the previous proposals. Specifically, develop an estimator that uses a novel sampling scheme, leverages the strengths of different kernel types, and employs a sophisticated dimensionality reduction technique. Evaluate the proposed estimator on a variety of datasets, and compare its performance to the results of existing estimators.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of the proposed estimator to the results of existing estimators, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and the hybrid approach.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: The proposed estimator should significantly improve the performance of existing estimators for Shapley values, especially on large and complex datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Multimodal Transformers to CNN-LSTM combinations for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: We will train and evaluate the performance of two competitive baselines on the task of temporal change description: a) a multimodal transformer model (specifically, a pre-trained MLLM fine-tuned on a large satellite image and text dataset), and b) a CNN-LSTM pipeline that leversages the strengths of both convolutional neural networks for image feature extraction and long short-term memory cells for modeling temporal dynamics. We will use large-scale, real-world satellite image datasets such as the Google Earth Engine's Landsat 8 dataset, and summarize performance using metrics such as SAM (self-assessment metric), ExpertJudgment, and average recall of key change events.
CONTROLS: This experiment compares two competitive baselines and uses real-world data with no ablation studies.
COST: 773
PREDICTION: The multimodal transformer model is expected to outperform the CNN-LSTM pipeline in terms of overall descriptive coherence and recall of key change events, particularly on tasks requiring deeper semantic understanding; however, the CNN-LSTM pipeline may excel in detecting local changes and transient events, which the transformer model might struggle to capture due to its focus on global patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Long-Range Temporal Causal Understanding via Interpretable Self-Attention
PROPOSAL: We will investigate a variant of the multimodal transformer model (specifically, the base model used in proposal 1) with an added explanatory neural behavioral analysis layer that identifies the most important causal factors of changes across the historical sequence. This will be achieved by interpreting the weights and patterns learned by the model's self-attention mechanism, highlighting which input features (e.g., image patches, metadata) and temporal relationships are most influential in driving predictions. We hypothesize that incorporating explicit causal understanding will further improve performance on temporal change description and unlock novel potential for temporal consistency in future forecasting.
CONTROLS: This experiment involves modifying an existing architecture and evaluating its performance on real-world data alongside the previously proposed comparison with CNN-LSTM.
COST: 3627
PREDICTION: The new model is expected to not only match but surpass all baseline models in capturing the underlying drivers of change, resulting in more coherent and semantically rich descriptions of dynamic events. However, its significantly higher computational cost might hamper performance on certain hardware or when dealing with large, dense data sequences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will introduce a novel evaluation metric for assessing temporal consistency in future satellite image forecasting, which combines traditional image quality metrics (e.g., SSIM, PSNR) with historical coherence metrics (e.g., SAM, KL-divergence) to ensure that forecasts are not only realistic but also logically consistent with observed trends. We will apply this metric to forecasts generated by the multimodal transformer models (including the causal variant from proposal 2) and compare them to state-of-the-art temporal forecasting methods that rely on low-level conditioning (e.g., edge maps, single-image synthesis).
CONTROLS: This experiment compares proposed models to both strong baselines and state-of-the-art methods on a novel evaluation metric for temporal consistency, and uses real-world data.
COST: 5191
PREDICTION: The causal variant of the multimodal transformer model is expected to significantly outperform other models in terms of temporal consistency, as its explicit understanding of causal drivers enables more coherent forecasting. However, the lack of strong baselines specifically optimized for temporal consistency might make the evaluation less rigorous than expected.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting using Synthetic Data
PROPOSAL: To better isolate the impact of temporal consistency, we will modify proposal 3 to utilize a large-scale, synthetic satellite image dataset with precisely controlled temporal trends and variability. This will enable a more rigorous evaluation of the proposed models' ability to capture and forecast temporal consistency under idealized conditions, allowing us to systematically explore the effects of various temporal dynamics and forecasting horizon lengths on performance.
CONTROLS: This experiment controls for external factors by using a controlled synthetic dataset and ensures that the evaluation is isolated to the forecasting algorithms and their performance on temporal consistency.
COST: 9162
PREDICTION: The causal variant of the multimodal transformer model should exhibit improved temporal consistency across a wide range of synthetic data scenarios, narrowly outperforming other models in settings where straightforward, deterministic temporal patterns dominate. However, as the complexity of the synthetic data increases (e.g., introducing non-linear relationships, stochastic processes), the model's overall performance may degrade due to overfitting to the learned patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Temporal Sampling Density on Model Performance
PROPOSAL: We will investigate how different temporal sampling densities (e.g., widely spaced, densely sampled, sparse) in our satellite image datasets affect the performance of the proposed models, particularly in terms of capturing long-range temporal dynamics. To this end, we will select several real-world satellite image datasets with varying sampling densities and train the causal multimodal transformer model on each of them. We hypothesize that the model's performance will degrade as the sampling density increases (i.e., fewer data points), necessitating the development of more robust and data-efficient methods.
CONTROLS: This experiment varies the sampling density of real-world datasets and evaluates the impact on model performance.
COST: 7285
PREDICTION: As expected, the model's performance will indeed degrade with decreasing sampling density, with significant drops in performance observed when the gap between consecutive observations increases. However, we also anticipate that the causal variant of the multimodal transformer model will be more resilient to data scarcity than its non-causal counterpart, particularly in capturing key short-term trends.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Comparing Multimodal Transformers to CNN-LSTM combinations for Temporal Change Description: Ablation Study
PROPOSAL: To better understand the effectiveness of multimodal transformers in capturing temporal change descriptions, we will perform an ablation study on the architecture proposed in proposal 1. Specifically, we will vary the number of transformer layers, the size of the transformer's attention heads, and the capacity of the cross-modal fusion module to understand which components are most critical for capturing key changes. This will guide the development of more efficient and effective models for temporal change description.
CONTROLS: This ablation study will provide a thorough analysis of model component contributions, ensuring that any future modifications or improvements are well-informed and validated.
COST: 1361
PREDICTION: The ablation study should reveal that a reduced number of transformer layers and smaller attention heads do not significantly impact overall performance, suggesting that the model's effectiveness in capturing temporal change descriptions is largely robust to minor architectural modifications. However, we also anticipate that the capacity of the cross-modal fusion module plays a crucial role in overall performance, necessitating its further refinement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Hyperparameter Tuning for Improved Temporal Consistency in Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop a dynamic hyperparameter tuning strategy tailored to the task of future satellite image forecasting, with a focus on optimizing hyperparameters that influence temporal consistency. Specifically, we will use a combination of Bayesian optimization and gradient-based methods to adaptively tune the hyperparameters of the causal multimodal transformer model, aiming to achieve improved forecasting performance on datasets with complex temporal dynamics.
CONTROLS: This experiment will compare the performance of the model with adaptive hyperparameter tuning to that of a baseline model with fixed hyperparameters, and utilize a comprehensive set of hyperparameter search spaces to ensure thorough exploration.
COST: 10928
PREDICTION: The dynamic hyperparameter tuning strategy should lead to a noticeable improvement in forecasting performance, particularly in capturing subtle changes in temporal trends and variability. However, we also anticipate that the increased complexity of the optimization process may lead to longer training times and potentially increased risk of overfitting.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting using Synthetic Data: A Control Flow Analysis Approach
PROPOSAL: To gain deeper insights into the behavior of the causal multimodal transformer model under varying temporal conditions, we will introduce a control flow analysis framework to visualize and understand the internal workings of the model during forecasting. This will enable us to identify specific patterns and correlations that contribute to improved temporal consistency, and provide a detailed understanding of how the model adapts to different forecasting scenarios.
CONTROLS: This revised experiment leverages a novel control flow analysis framework to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the model's behavior, ensuring that any conclusions drawn are well-founded and offer deep insights into the forecasting process.
COST: 20253
PREDICTION: The control flow analysis approach should reveal that the causal multimodal transformer model effectively captures key temporal patterns and correlations, particularly in datasets with complex, non-linear dynamics. However, we also anticipate that the increased complexity of the analysis may lead to a rise in computational costs, potentially impacting the model's real-world deployment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multitask Learning for Enhanced Change Understanding and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: To tackle the task of simultaneous change understanding and forecasting, we will train a multitask model that jointly learns to describe past changes and forecast future scenes from satellite image time series data. Using a combination of multimodal transformers and causal reasoning, we aim to develop a unified architecture that can tackle both tasks effectively and efficiently. We will evaluate this approach on benchmarks for both change description and forecasting, comparing its performance against competitive baselines and ablated versions of itself.
CONTROLS: This experiment will serve as a direct comparison between multitask learning and single-task training, controlling for various hyperparameters and architectural components to understand the contribution of multitask learning to overall performance.
COST: 25109
PREDICTION: The multitask model should achieve competitive or even superior performance on both change description and forecasting tasks compared to single-task models, due to its shared architecture and learned representations across tasks. However, we also anticipate that training a multitask model may lead to increased risk of adversarial effects between tasks, potentially causing performance drops in either task if not properly aligned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation Metrics for Assessing Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Given the limitations of traditional image quality metrics for evaluating temporal consistency, we will propose a set of novel evaluation metrics tailored to assess the temporal coherence of satellite image forecasts. These metrics will combine quantitative measures of prediction consistency, trend alignment, and evolution likelihood to effectively evaluate the long-term predictability of satellite image time series data. We will implement and test these metrics on a range of satellite image forecasting datasets and models, aiming to establish a new standard for temporal consistency evaluation in this field.
CONTROLS: This experiment will serve as a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed evaluation metrics, directly comparing their performance to existing metrics and ensuring that the new metrics capture meaningful aspects of temporal coherence in satellite image forecasts.
COST: 30567
PREDICTION: The proposed evaluation metrics should provide a more nuanced and comprehensive understanding of temporal consistency in satellite image forecasting, enabling more accurate model evaluation and selection. However, we also anticipate that developing and validating these metrics will require significant domain expertise and iterative refinement to ensure that they accurately capture the complexities of long-term predictability in satellite image time series data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Adapter Architectures on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of different adapter architectures (e.g. 1D convolutional adapter, multi-layer perceptron adapter) in an online time series forecasting setting. Our experiment will train and evaluate these adapters on the M4 forecasting dataset, which covers various time series forecasting tasks including traffic flow, electricity consumption, and temperature forecasting. For this study, we will estimate our results using the symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) metric. Baseline models will include an adaptation of the popular Prophet model using a single-layer perceptron as a fixed adapter.
CONTROLS: Baseline models include Prophet with a single-layer perceptron adapter, OGD on the final prediction layer of a deep forecasting model.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect the 1D convolutional adapter to outperform the single-layer perceptron adapter, and both to outperform the baseline models. Failure could occur due to poor hyperparameter tuning, difficulty in scaling the architecture to varying data distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Normalization Strategies in Mitigating Distribution Shift
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of different normalization strategies (e.g. layer normalization, instance normalization, learnable normalization) on online time series forecasting. Our experiment will train and evaluate these models on the same M4 forecasting dataset as before. To control for the potential impact of these normalization strategies, we will evaluate their performance under various distribution shift scenarios, including covariate shift and concept drift.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will be the same as in Proposal 1, and we will also evaluate the effectiveness of strategy combination and adaptive normalization methods.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: We expect normalization to mitigate the impact of distribution shift on forecasting accuracy, with some strategies performing better than others depending on the specific shift scenario. However, failure could occur if the shift is too abrupt or unpredictable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Gradient Extrapolation Methods for Improved Online Forecasting Accuracy
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effectiveness of gradient extrapolation methods (e.g., Nesterov acceleration, Polyak-Ruppert average) for improving online forecasting accuracy. Our experiment will train and evaluate these methods on the M4 forecasting dataset. To control for the impact of these methods, we will also evaluate their performance on a synthetic dataset with induced concept drift.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include online gradient descent (OGD), and we will evaluate the impact of gradient extrapolation methods on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect gradient extrapolation methods to improve online forecasting accuracy, especially in the presence of concept drift. However, failure could occur if these methods exacerbate the high variance of gradients estimated from few samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Update Scheduling for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of adaptive update scheduling on online time series forecasting. Our experiment will train and evaluate a model that dynamically adjusts the update frequency based on the history of forecasting errors. This adaptation will be done by a secondary MLP that takes into account the errors, the granularity of the predictions and the temporal alignment between training and prediction set. For validation, we will use the M4 forecasting dataset.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include OGD with fixed update frequency, and we will evaluate the impact of adaptive scheduling on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: We expect adaptive update scheduling to improve online forecasting accuracy, especially in scenarios with concept drift. However, failure could occur if the adaptive scheduling mechanism becomes overly complex or difficult to tune.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Online Forecasting with Adaptable Parameters
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach for online forecasting with adaptable parameters. The approach involves pre-training a base model on a set of synthetic datasets with varying distribution shifts, and then fine-tuning the adaptable parameters on the target dataset. Our experiment will train and evaluate this approach on a set of real-world datasets from various domains (traffic flow, electricity consumption, weather forecasting). To control for the impact of the adaptable parameters, we will also evaluate the performance of the approach on fixed parameters.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include OGD with fixed and adaptive scheduling, and we will evaluate the impact of the adaptable parameters on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 48000
PREDICTION: We expect the meta-learning approach to improve online forecasting accuracy, especially in scenarios with concept drift. However, failure could occur if the pre-training step does not adequately prepare the model for the target distribution shift.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: A Deeper Look into Meta-Learning for Online Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We refine our meta-learning approach for online forecasting by incorporating a more complex architecture, where the adaptable parameters are learned using a secondary meta-model. Our experiment will train and evaluate this refined approach on a set of real-world datasets from various domains (traffic flow, electricity consumption, weather forecasting). We also evaluate the approach on a cognitive assessment, to understand its ability to self-assess its own confidence, init/trigger adapt/avoid exploratory updates in adversarial conditions. 
CONTROLS: Baseline models remain the same as before.
COST: 60000 (increased complexity necessitates more compute power)
PREDICTION: We expect the refined meta-learning approach to further improve online forecasting accuracy, and exhibit improved robustness and adaptability in scenarios with concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Multi-Step Forecasting on Online Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of multi-step forecasting on online forecasting accuracy. Our experiment will compare the performance of single-step and multi-step forecasting methods on a set of real-world datasets from various domains (traffic flow, electricity consumption, weather forecasting). We will also evaluate the impact of different forecasting horizon lengths on online forecasting accuracy.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include OGD with fixed and adaptive scheduling, and we will evaluate the impact of multi-step forecasting on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: We expect multi-step forecasting to improve online forecasting accuracy, especially when the forecasting horizon is short. However, failure could occur if the multi-step forecasting approach exacerbates the high variance of gradients estimated from few samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Adaptive Update Scheduling for Online Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of adaptive update scheduling for online forecasting, focusing on the expected regret and convergence rate. Our analysis will derive new bounds on the adaptive update scheduling algorithm and compare them to existing bounds on OGD.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include OGD with fixed and adaptive scheduling, and we will evaluate the impact of adaptive update scheduling on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 70000
PREDICTION: Our theoretical analysis will provide a deeper understanding of the adaptive update scheduling algorithm and its limitations, and will inform the design of future online forecasting algorithms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Practical Implementation of Online Forecasting with Gradient- Based Methods and Directly Adaptive Models
PROPOSAL: We explore the practical implementation of online forecasting with gradient-based methods (e.g. OGD, gradient extrapolation) and directly adaptive models (e.g. meta-learning, online eigendecomposition). Our experiment will compare the performance of these methods on a set of real-world datasets from various domains (traffic flow, electricity consumption, weather forecasting). We will also evaluate the impact of different model complexities on online forecasting accuracy.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include fixed update scheduling and no adaptation, and we will evaluate the impact of adaptive scheduling and model adaptation on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 110000
PREDICTION: We expect gradient-based methods to perform well on datasets with smooth distribution shifts, while directly adaptive models will perform better on datasets with abrupt concept drift.

ACTION: REVISE 8
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation of Online Forecasting Algorithms on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: We combine and extend the results from our previous experiments to provide a comprehensive evaluation of online forecasting algorithms on real-world datasets from various domains (traffic flow, electricity consumption, weather forecasting). Our comprehensive evaluation will include a comparison of gradient-based methods (OGD, gradient extrapolation) and directly adaptive models (meta-learning, online eigendecomposition) with different adaptive update scheduling schemes and model complexities.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include fixed update scheduling and no adaptation, and we will evaluate the impact of adaptive scheduling and model adaptation on both covariate shift and concept drift scenarios.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: Our comprehensive evaluation will provide valuable insights into the performance of online forecasting algorithms on real-world datasets and inform the design of future online forecasting systems.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of a Lightweight Dense Text retriever on Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of a multimodal retriever that combines a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder with a lightweight dense text retriever, such as the Annoy implementation of FAISS, on a dataset like Document Retrieval from Camera Phone Images (DRCI) or a similar visual document retrieval benchmark.
CONTROLS: Compare the combined model with the ColPali-base encoder alone, as well as with a strong baseline of single-vector dense text retriever.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Improving the trade-off between retrieval quality and online latency, and showing whether a lightweight dense text retriever can complement a stronger vision-centric retriever. Potential failure: the combined model may perform worse than the ColPali-base encoder if the dense text retriever is too weak or adds too much latency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Aggregation Schemes for Heterogeneous Multimodal Representations
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate several aggregation schemes that can combine the outputs of a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder and a lightweight dense text retriever at the representation level, while respecting strict latency and memory budgets. This includes investigating techniques like concatenation, averaging, and element-wise multiplication, as well as more sophisticated methods such as neural factura aggregation or learned heavy hitters.
CONTROLS: Compare the effectiveness of different aggregation schemes, as well as their impact on retrieval quality, online latency, and index memory, using the combined model from proposal 1.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: Identifying the most effective aggregation scheme and understanding its limitations, as well as demonstrating the practicality of aggregation-based multimodal retrieval. Potential failure: the aggregation schemes may not perform well enough to surpass the baseline models or may introduce additional complexity that hinders their adoption.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Impact of Weighting on Aggregation Schemes
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of learned and fixed weightings on the aggregation schemes proposed in proposal 2, with the goal of identifying how to optimize the combination of vision-centric and dense text retriever outputs. This includes designing a weighting module that takes into account the confidence of the individual retrievers and their relevance to the query.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of different weighting strategies, including learned and fixed weightings, on the aggregation schemes, as well as their impact on retrieval quality, online latency, and index memory.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: Developing a more robust and adaptive aggregation approach that can handle the heterogeneity of multimodal representations and improve multimodal retrieval performance. Potential failure: the weighing module may not perform well or require significant computational resources, affecting the overall feasibility of the approach.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of a Lightweight Dense Text retriever on Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders with Different Query Types
PROPOSAL: Refine proposal 1 by investigating how a lightweight dense text retriever affects the performance of a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder on different types of queries, such as short and long queries, or queries with varying levels of relevance to the visual content. This will help understand whether the combination of models is effective across different scenarios.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the combined model on different query types with the ColPali-base encoder alone, as well as with a strong baseline of single-vector dense text retriever.
COST: 5040
PREDICTION: Understanding the limitations and strengths of combining a lightweight dense text retriever with a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder on different types of queries and adapting the combination approach to improve performance. Potential failure: the combination may not perform well on long or complex queries, or may require tuning for each query type, affecting its practicality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Multimodal Retrieval under Heterogeneity
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of the multimodal retrieval problem under heterogeneity, where different retrievers have various dimensionalities and scales. This includes analyzing the quality of the aggregation function under different types of heterogeneity and providing guarantees on the performance of the combined retriever.
CONTROLS: Compare the theoretical results with empirical results from proposals 1, 2, and 3, to validate the practicality of the analysis.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: Developing a thorough theoretical understanding of multimodal retrieval under heterogeneity and providing insights on the design of aggregation schemes that can effectively handle various types of heterogeneity. Potential failure: the theoretical analysis may not align with empirical results or may not provide tractable solutions that can be implemented in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Implementation of Multimodal Retrieval with Heterogeneous Aggregation
PROPOSAL: Design and optimize an efficient implementation of the multimodal retrieval system that combines a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder with a lightweight dense text retriever and heterogeneous aggregation, leveraging parallel processing and low-precision arithmetic to reduce computational complexity and memory usage.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance and efficiency of the optimized implementation on a range of hardware platforms and compare it to the baseline models.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Developing a highly efficient and scalable implementation of multimodal retrieval that can handle large-scale datasets and real-world applications, and providing a practical solution for the limitations of single-model approaches. Potential failure: the optimized implementation may introduce new performance bottlenecks or memory constraints, or may require significant re-optimization for different hardware platforms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparative Study on BM25 and Dense Text Retrievers for Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Perform a comparative study on the effectiveness of BM25 and dense text retrievers in multimodal retrieval, including evaluating their performance on a range of datasets and queries, and analyzing the impact of parameter tuning on their performance.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of BM25 and dense text retrievers with the multimodal retriever proposed in proposal 1, and investigate the effectiveness of combining BM25 and dense text retrievers for multimodal retrieval.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: Understanding the relative strengths and weaknesses of BM25 and dense text retrievers for multimodal retrieval and identifying the best approach for different use cases, and providing insights on the role of dense text retrievers in multimodal retrieval. Potential failure: the comparative study may not reveal significant differences between BM25 and dense text retrievers, or may require extensive parameter tuning and tuning datasets specific to the task.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Efficient Implementation of Multimodal Retrieval with Heterogeneous Aggregation for Large-Scale Datasets
PROPOSAL: Refine proposal 5 by designing and optimizing a distributed and parallelized implementation of the multimodal retrieval system that can handle large-scale datasets and heterogeneous aggregation, leveraging popular distributed computing frameworks and job scheduling systems to optimize resource utilization.
